helpers.name: search_directives

parameters.name: keyword
parameters.description: Free-text search over directive names, descriptions, and intent keywords, one or more words (e.g. 'task decomposition')

helpers.purpose: Find directives by type, category, or keyword when you know the domain but not the exact directive name. Multi-word input is split into words; a row matches if ANY word prefix-matches ("disk space free" finds get_free_disk_space). Rows matching more words rank first. Punctuation is ignored, so no FTS syntax is needed or honored. Common stopwords (the, of, and, ...) are ignored unless the query is nothing but stopwords. Keyword results are ordered by name/description relevance.
helpers.error_handling: Returns empty array if no matches found
return_statements: Directives exist for ALL aspects of AIMFP — if you're unsure how to handle a workflow step, there is almost certainly a directive for it. Search by keyword or type to find relevant guidance. Do NOT assume you know the workflow from memory — load and follow the directive.
For full workflow details on a matched directive, call get_directive_by_name(name). For deep edge-case context, call get_directive_content(name) to read the MD documentation.
implementation_notes: Returns: Array of matching directive objects with workflow, description, category, etc.
Implementation should also query and include directive-specific preferences from directive_preferences table (if any exist for each directive)

used_by_directives.description: User searches for directives by keyword or topic

helpers.name: get_flows_from_directive
helpers.purpose: Get all flows originating from a directive (what comes next?). Returns raw flow data - AI evaluates conditions.
helpers.error_handling: Returns empty array if no flows found
return_statements: Directive flows define the directive-to-directive navigation system — 'what directive comes next' based on current state. Evaluate the condition_key/condition_value fields against current project state to determine which directive flow to follow. Do NOT guess the next directive from memory — use get_flows_from_directive.

After identifying the next directive from directive flows, load it via get_directive_by_name before executing. Directives contain step-by-step workflow guidance — always read them from the database, never execute from cached memory.
NOTE: Directive flows (directive_flow table in aimfp_core.db) are distinct from project flows (flow_themes/file_flows in project.db). This tool queries directive flows only.
implementation_notes: Simple query: SELECT * FROM directive_flow WHERE from_directive = ? ORDER BY priority
Returns all flow fields including condition_key, condition_value for AI to evaluate
Does NOT evaluate conditions - AI determines which path to take based on its knowledge of project state
Includes wildcard flows if from_directive='*' is queried directly

helpers.name: get_flows_to_directive
helpers.purpose: Get all directive flows leading to a directive (what leads here?). Useful for understanding directive prerequisites.
helpers.error_handling: Returns empty array if no directive flows found
return_statements: Directive flows show which directives route to this one and under what conditions. Use to understand prerequisites and entry points for any directive workflow.
NOTE: Directive flows (aimfp_core.db) are distinct from project flows (project.db flow_themes/file_flows).
implementation_notes: Simple query: SELECT * FROM directive_flow WHERE to_directive = ? ORDER BY priority
Returns all flow fields
Useful for: understanding what triggers a directive, finding entry points

helpers.name: get_fp_directive_index
helpers.purpose: Get lightweight FP directive index grouped by category (names only, not full definitions)
helpers.error_handling: Returns empty object if no FP directives found
return_statements: FP directives are REFERENCE material for when AI is uncertain about implementation details - consult as needed, not mandatory execution paths
AI writes FP code naturally as baseline behavior - only consult these directives when genuinely uncertain
No strict workflows with FP directives - they're available on-demand for guidance on complex FP patterns (monads, currying, lazy evaluation, etc.)
implementation_notes: Returns: {category_name: [directive_name, ...]}
Example: {'error_handling': ['fp_optionals', 'fp_result_types'], 'purity': ['fp_purity', 'fp_immutability']}
Query: SELECT d.name, c.name as category FROM directives d JOIN directive_categories dc ON d.id=dc.directive_id JOIN categories c ON dc.category_id=c.id WHERE d.type='fp' ORDER BY c.name, d.name
Groups by category name
Lightweight: ~1-2k tokens vs ~10-15k for full FP flows
Does NOT return full directive definitions or flows - just names grouped by category
Use search_directives(type='fp') or get_directive_by_name(name) for full details

used_by_directives.description: Called by aimfp_run when is_new_session=true - provides FP directive quick reference grouped by category

helpers.name: get_directive_flows
helpers.purpose: General-purpose query for directive flows by category, type, or directive names. Complements the navigation helpers (get_flows_from_directive, get_flows_to_directive, get_wildcard_flows), which answer where a specific directive routes.
helpers.error_handling: Returns empty array if no flows match filters
return_statements: When flow_category='fp': These are CONSULTATION flows - FP directives are reference material for when AI needs guidance, not mandatory execution workflows
FP flows show available reference directives, not required execution paths - AI consults them on-demand when uncertain about complex FP patterns
implementation_notes: Returns: Array of flow objects with all fields (id, from_directive, to_directive, flow_category, flow_type, condition_key, condition_value, condition_description, priority, description)
All parameters are optional - can combine filters for targeted queries
Example: get_directive_flows(flow_category='fp') returns all FP consultation flows
Example: get_directive_flows(flow_category='git', flow_type='conditional') returns git conditional flows
Query: SELECT * FROM directive_flow WHERE 1=1 [AND flow_category=?] [AND flow_type=?] [AND from_directive=?] [AND to_directive=?]
Complements existing navigation helpers which are workflow-focused (what's next during execution)
Use for: Browsing flows by category, analyzing flow structure, debugging, querying specific flow paths
Differs from get_next_directives_from_status: That evaluates conditions for workflow navigation, this is pure query

helpers.name: get_wildcard_flows
helpers.purpose: Get all directive flows from wildcard '*' source (available from ANY context). Includes FP references, utilities, cross-cutting concerns.
helpers.error_handling: Returns empty array if no directive flows found
return_statements: Wildcard directive flows are available from ANY directive context — they represent cross-cutting concerns like FP reference consultation and utility directives. Load the target directive via get_directive_by_name before executing.
NOTE: These are directive flows (aimfp_core.db), distinct from project flows (project.db flow_themes/file_flows).
implementation_notes: Simple query: SELECT * FROM directive_flow WHERE from_directive = '*' [AND flow_type = ?] ORDER BY flow_type, priority
Wildcard '*' means: available from ANY directive context (not sequential workflow)
Common flow_types for wildcards: 'reference_consultation' (FP references), 'utility' (cross-cutting utilities)
If flow_type not provided, returns ALL wildcard flows
AI uses this to find what's available regardless of current workflow position

helpers.name: get_directive_content
helpers.purpose: Read and return the full MD documentation file for a directive. Resolves the md_file_path from aimfp_core.db to an absolute path within the installed package, reads the file, and returns content + absolute path + token estimate.
helpers.error_handling: Returns error if directive not found, md_file_path is null, or file cannot be read
return_statements: Returns directive MD content, absolute file path, and token estimate. MD documentation is the DEEPEST layer of directive guidance — it contains complete workflows, examples, edge cases, FP compliance notes, and cross-directive relationships.

Use for: complex edge cases, ambiguity in workflow steps, FP compliance questions, cross-directive relationships, and any situation where the JSON workflow steps from get_directive_by_name are not sufficient.

Directives cover ALL aspects of AIMFP. If you're uncertain about any workflow — file operations, interactions, types, reserve/finalize, task management, FP patterns — there is a directive with detailed guidance. Read it before improvising.
implementation_notes: Looks up md_file_path from directives table in aimfp_core.db
Resolves to absolute path: Path(__file__).parent.parent.parent / 'reference' / md_file_path
Reads file with UTF-8 encoding, estimates tokens at ~1 token per 4 characters
Returns Result with data={content, absolute_path, token_estimate, directive_name}
Largest directive MD is ~27KB (~7K tokens), most are 8-23KB (2-6K tokens)
